newsitem.title: UK: Five hundred more troops for troubled N.Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Five hundred more troops for troubled N.Ireland.

text.p: Five hundred more British troops are being sent to Northern Ireland to help fight a tide of violence, security officials said on Wednesday.
They said the troops would be used to combat terrorism and join 18,000 British soldiers already serving in the province.
An army spokesman said the additional troops would help the local Royal Ulster Constabulary police "combat terrorism and ensure law and order". They would arrive within 48 hours.
The province has been gripped by nightly rioting since Britain allowed the Protestant Orange Order to parade down the Catholic Garvaghy Road area of Portadown last Sunday.
It is also gripped by concern at two more Protestant parades in Belfast and Londonderry on Saturday, the 12th of July, which marks the climax of the Protestants' annual "marching season".
